extracted.subtask_description: Reporting frontline and home-front wartime events in newspaper dispatch format: datelined reports that synthesize official communiques, radio broadcasts, eyewitness accounts, and agency dispatches into a single article. Emphasizes attribution, numbers, and strategic context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline and time stamping
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a clear dateline and date (e.g., "London, Wednesday, March 10", "Moscow, March 9") to establish when and where the report originates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use city and date lines for each distinct dispatch within a story so readers can track timing and location of separate reports; helps indicate timeliness and separate agency inputs (examples in text: London, Moscow, Africa datelines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate source attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Attribute claims and facts to named sources: radio, official communiques, broadcasts, or agencies (e.g., "The German radio declared...", "The British communique said...", "By the Associated Press").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label the source of each claim so readers can judge reliability; distinguish between official communiques, enemy broadcasts, and agency/field reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present opposing/contrasting accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Report both sides' claims and clearly label them (for example, German claims of damage or numbers vs. Allied communiques and losses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When conflicting reports exist (e.g., casualty or damage counts), present each side's version and avoid asserting one as fact unless corroborated; use headings or phrases such as 'Germans Claim...' to flag partisan claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify casualties, losses and equipment when available
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide specific numbers for casualties, planes shot down, tanks abandoned, tons of supplies, etc. (examples: "thirty-three were killed", "fifty wrecked tanks", detailed lend-lease tonnages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give exact figures when reported, but indicate whether they are estimates, claims, or confirmed counts; when multiple figures appear, note source and caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag uncertainty and unconfirmed details
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate uncertainty explicitly (e.g., "did not specify whether it was at Rouen or Rennes", "it was presumed here that...").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use words like 'presumed', 'reported', 'said', 'authoritative announcement' to mark unverified information; avoid definitive language for unconfirmed items and explain the ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use eyewitness quotes for immediacy and color
rubrics_metrics.description: Include short eyewitness or participant quotes where relevant (example: "A Canadian flyer on the raid said 'I saw one really ...'").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotes add human detail but should be attributed and kept concise; contextualize them with corroborating facts when possible to prevent undue weight on a single observer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite official communiques and interpret jargon
rubrics_metrics.description: Quote and, when helpful, explain terms used in official communiques (example: "the RAF was out 'in strength'—the term deemed to indicate that...").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using military or bureaucratic jargon from communiques, either quote the term and provide an interpretive gloss for general readers or contrast it with observed effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide strategic and logistical context
rubrics_metrics.description: Place tactical events in broader strategic frame and report logistic details that affect the campaign (examples: advances toward Vyazma, Dnieper River, lend-lease totals, supply shipments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why reported movements, losses or supply figures matter to the larger campaign; include comparisons and effects on frontlines or morale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate multiple agency/dispatch inputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine reporting from wire services and correspondents (e.g., Associated Press, Reuters) and mark their contributions (e.g., labels like '[By the Associated Press]' or 'Reuters reported...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When synthesizing several dispatches, keep attributions clear so readers know which agency provided which detail and to reflect differing emphases or access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report home-front and propaganda reactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover domestic broadcasts, press reactions and political statements (examples: Soviet broadcasts of Stettinius' statement, Nazi press seizing on American remarks, British official comments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include how statements and broadcasts are used for propaganda or public morale, and cite reactions from governments or press to show broader impact beyond the battlefield.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document civil unrest and resistance incidents with locations
rubrics_metrics.description: When covering guerrilla activity, reprisals or riots, name cities/regions and give incident counts or descriptions (examples: 'Scores of soldiers and Gestapo agents have been slain', 'Guerrillas of Lille killed twenty-three German officers').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete locations and approximate counts; attribute to sources and note reprisals or countermeasures to give a clear picture of scope and intensity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish confirmed sinking/damage from observed engagements
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate between observed air/sea engagements and confirmed sinkings or damage (e.g., 'Fortresses had sunk or damaged seven Axis ships in a convoy' vs. observed collisions or combats).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear whether claims of sinkings or damage are confirmed by multiple sources or remain battle claims; avoid conjoining combat claims with confirmed outcomes without attribution.
